## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply, or I explain the exception below.
- [x] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)).

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL

## Summary

cc 10.3 (B300 / GB300) had no placement-table entries, so every SM100-row graph there fell back to the hand rules, and the gb300 nightly showed the same default-dispatch losses as gb200 before #1957 / #2094. This PR lets cc 10.3 borrow the cc 10.0 entries, **study by study, only where a transfer check on a B300 qualified them**:

- `placement_table.PART_TRANSFERS[(10, 3)] = ((10, 0), {six studies})`. `lookup` falls back to the cc 10.0 entry of the same class only when that entry's study is listed.
- A later cc 10.0 study does **not** answer for cc 10.3 until a transfer check names it.
- An unmeasured part (cc 10.1 in the tests) keeps the hand rules.

## Why

### Method (study `sm103_transfer_20261031`)

B300 SXM6, 1100 W, cuDNN 9.29.0.17 (the nightly build). Cases were frozen (sha256) before timing.
- **Transfer sample (201 cases):** a cost-stratified sample of each listed study's frozen cc 10.0 grid, on and off the 128-key tile. It covers:
  - d256 decode, dense and paged;
  - paged D576 q1 / MTP;
  - paged d512 decode;
  - dense D576 decode;
  - paged d512 / d256 context, including the short-KV cells.
- **Holdout (56 cases):** off the training lattice (odd head counts and batches, off-tile lengths), scored once.
- **Scoring:** the full runtime placement (table plus hand rules) at cc 10.3, against develop's placement on the same graphs. Regret = chosen ÷ faster provider.

### Results

| Family | Transfer sample: this PR (geo / max) | Transfer sample: develop | Holdout: this PR | Holdout: develop |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| paged d512 decode | 1.000 / 1.000 | 2.980 / 13.4 | 1.000 | 3.186 |
| dense D576 decode | 1.000 / 1.000 | 2.733 / 11.4 | 1.000 | 2.079 |
| paged d512 context | 1.021 / 1.456 | 2.207 / 6.30 | 1.000 | 2.305 |
| paged d256 context | 1.025 / 1.322 | 1.499 / 4.72 | 1.000 | 1.949 |
| dense d256 decode | 1.003 / 1.114 | 1.159 / 6.89 | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| paged d256 decode | 1.000 / 1.010 | 1.035 / 1.61 | 1.000 | 1.064 |
| paged D576 q1 / MTP | 1.000 / 1.000 | 1.000 / 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 |

- 115 routes change; one is slower than develop: 1.11×, the 32-tile off-tile d256 boundary, which the cc 10.0 grid also measured as mixed (0.88–1.04).
- The context residuals are the same conservative short-KV cells as on cc 10.0.

**Out of sample, gb300 nightly run-496** (GB300, cuDNN 9.29, model shapes, used nowhere above), with the nightly's own backend / FROST times:

| Class | n | Nightly default (geo / max) | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| paged d512 decode | 24 | 3.83 / 13.1 | 1.000 |
| paged d512 context | 48 | 2.39 / 2.73 | 1.000 |
| paged d256 context | 28 | 1.62 / 1.85 | 1.000 |
| dense D576 decode | 8 | 2.42 / 6.41 | 1.018 |
| paged d256 decode | 12 | 1.15 / 1.63 | 1.000 |
| dense d256 decode | 40 | 1.07 / 1.68 | 1.001 |

## Related issues

Follows #1957 / #2094 (the cc 10.0 generated entries).

## API and compatibility impact

None to the API. Placement changes on cc 10.3 only, for the classes the six listed studies cover.

## Testing

- New `test_cc103_borrows_only_the_studies_its_transfer_check_named`:
  - cc 10.3 answers like cc 10.0 for the covered classes;
  - a cc 10.0 entry from an unlisted study does not transfer.
- Tests that used cc 10.3 as "an unmeasured part" now use cc 10.1.
- `pytest -m "" sdpa/frost/test_placement_table.py sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_fwd_placement.py sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_fwd_heuristics.py sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_bwd_heuristics.py core`: 1056 passed. The one failure, `core/graph/test_kernel_cache.py::test_serialize_both_graph_and_kernel_cache`, fails identically on develop on this host.
- Not covered: backward on cc 10.3. #1944's d256 backward lead is a cc 10.0 hand rule; gb300 shows d256 backward 1.16–1.33 on the backend. That needs a training-harness transfer check.

+PART_TRANSFERS: Dict[Tuple[int, int], Tuple[Tuple[int, int], FrozenSet[str]]] = {
+    # study sm103_transfer_20261031 (B300 SXM6 1100 W, cuDNN 9.29.0.17): a cost-stratified sample of each listed study's frozen
+    # cc 10.0 grid (201 cases) plus 56 off-lattice holdout cases, timed on cc 10.3 and scored through the full placement:

+    # cc 10.3 -- a new cc 10.0 study does not, until a transfer check names it here.
+    (10, 3): (
+        (10, 0),
+        frozenset(
+            {
+                "sm100_d256_decode_v3_20261028",
+                "sm100_d576_decode_v2_20261028",
+                "sm100_d512_paged_decode_b100_20261030",
+                "sm100_d512_paged_context_20261030",
+                "sm100_d256_paged_context_20261030",
+                "sm100_d576_dense_decode_20261030",
+            }
+        ),
+    ),
+}
+"""A part with no study of its own may borrow a measured part's entries, study by study, once a transfer check timed that
+study's classes on it."""
+
+
+def _answer(entry: Entry, facts) -> bool:
     if entry.direction in ("always", "never"):
         return entry.direction == "always"
     w = FEATURES[entry.feature](facts)
     return w >= entry.log2_work if entry.direction == "ge" else w <= entry.log2_work
 
 
+def lookup(row: str, facts) -> Optional[bool]:
+    key = class_key(row, facts)
+    if key is None:
+        return None
+    entry = TABLE.get(key)
+    if entry is not None:
+        return _answer(entry, facts)
+    if key[1] not in PART_TRANSFERS:
+        return None
+    base, studies = PART_TRANSFERS[key[1]]
+    entry = TABLE.get(key[:1] + (base,) + key[2:])
+    if entry is None or entry.study not in studies:
+        return None
+    return _answer(entry, facts)
+
+
